extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners (Korean Patent Office), patent attorneys and applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on classifying and preparing notices/decisions of rejection (final vs non-final), conducting claim-by-claim examination, drafting written notices/decisions, and how to cite prior art in rejection documents for patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision where amended claim identical to previously-notified rejected claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amended claim is identical to the other claim to which a ground of rejection was notified, a decision to reject shall be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amended claim duplicates claim language that previously had a ground of rejection notified, treat the amended claim as not overcoming the notified ground and prepare a decision to reject rather than a non-final notice. (See examples where newly added claim identical to an earlier-notified indefinite claim results in a decision to reject.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of notice of grounds for rejection (final vs non-final)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of grounds for rejection can be classified into two types: (1) final rejection necessitated by the amendments made in response to the previously-issued rejection ('final rejection necessitated by amendment'); and (2) non-final rejection which is not the final rejection necessitated by amendment ('non-final rejection').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The type of notice affects applicant's permitted scope of amendments and subsequent procedure. Determination depends on whether the ground for rejection arose because of applicant's amendments (final) or for reasons other than amendments / existed before amendment (non-final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final rejection: when to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may issue 'non-final rejection' regardless of voluntary amendments if it is issued for the first time since the start of examination; where an unamended portion of the specification includes a ground for rejection; or when the ground for rejection is due to the description/claims before amendment rather than being necessitated by amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific points: (1) Issue non-final even if voluntary amendments exist when it's the first notice in examination; (2) If unamended specification portions include grounds, issue non-final; (3) If grounds after amendment are attributable to pre-amendment deficiencies, issue non-final; (4) Grounds arising for reasons other than amendments (e.g., change in foreigner's capacity) are non-final; (5) In ex-officio re-examination or remanded applications, certain grounds that might otherwise be 'necessitated by amendment' may be issued as non-final to avoid unfairly limiting applicants. Examples illustrate amended claim becoming examinable for novelty/inventive step but still treated as non-final when ground existed prior to amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection necessitated by amendment: when to issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ground for rejection arises from amendments made in response to a previously-notified rejection, the examiner shall issue the final rejection necessitated by the amendment. Amendments in response to a prior notice are a prerequisite; final rejection can only be issued when a written amendment has been submitted and a new ground for rejection incurred in that amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical examples: (1) Amendments add new matter or exceed permissible scope of division/conversion; (2) Claim amendments cause grounds regarding novelty or inventive step that did not exist prior to amendment (unless the amended invention is the same as another claim never notified); (3) Newly added claims or claims changed equivalent to new claims that contain novelty/inventive step grounds (unless identical to an uninvolved claim); (4) After amendment, claim becomes examinable for novelty/inventive step due to removal of clarity issues or addition of new matter. Examples show adding element D creating a new need to rely on prior art including D, thereby producing a final rejection necessitated by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rule between final and non-final notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner discovers a ground for rejection after re-examination, he/she shall issue the non-final rejection unless all of the grounds for rejection fall under final rejection necessitated by the amendment. If uncertainty exists between the two types, the examiner shall issue the non-final rejection to avoid unreasonably limiting the applicant's opportunity to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to non-final when any doubt exists or when not all grounds are clearly caused by amendment; this protects applicant amendment rights and avoids premature limitation of amendment scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of claim-by-claim examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner examines applications to ensure patentability requirements are met and to enable an applicant to identify which claims are remediable. When notifying grounds for rejection in multi-claim applications, the examiner shall specify the claim containing the ground and provide specific explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim-by-claim examination helps applicants determine which claims to delete or amend and avoids inadvertently losing patentable claims. Notices should be specific per claim rather than blanket statements covering multiple claims without per-claim reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice structure and required parts
rubrics_metrics.description: A written notice of grounds for rejection (Examination Report) shall include: 'Claims to be Examined', 'Relevant Provisions regarding Grounds for Rejection', 'Patentable Claims', and 'Specific Grounds for Rejection'. Matters not forming grounds but useful for applicant response may be included in 'Considerations of Amendment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each part has specific content expectations (see separate rubric entries). The notice should enable the applicant to respond effectively by providing claim numbers, legal provisions, per-claim grounds, and helpful considerations for amendment. Avoid mixing up materials that are intended only as considerations vs actual grounds—if intending to use considerations as grounds, notify again as grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims to be Examined content
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Claims to be Examined' shall stipulate the number(s) of claims to be examined as of the date when the written notice is prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly list claim numbers included in the current examination scope so applicants know exactly which claims are under scrutiny in this report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant Provisions regarding Grounds for Rejection content
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Relevant Provisions regarding Grounds for Rejection' specifies claims containing grounds for rejection and the relevant provisions of the Act. If the ground is not directly related to claims, the matters containing the ground for rejection are stated here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an amendment adds new matter or exceeds scope for divisional/converted applications, state that the newly added matters or those falling outside scope are grounds for rejection and cite the statutory provision (e.g., Article numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable Claims entry rules
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Patentable Claim' enumerates all claims not identified as grounds for rejection upon notice. It is not the examiner's final decision and may be changed if new grounds later arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: a claim may be omitted from 'Patentable Claims' even if not identified as a ground where special circumstances make assessing patentability difficult, or where the claim is unpatentable due to other related grounds. If omitted, explain reasons in 'Considerations of Amendment'. The 'Patentable Claims' entry helps applicants choose which claims to keep or delete in subsequent procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Grounds for Rejection: per-claim specificity and prior-art comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Specific Grounds for Rejection' stipulates specific reasons for notified grounds, and examiners shall specifically state grounds for each claim, identifying which parts of prior art are used and how they compare to claimed features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance includes: (i) state grounds per claim (or group claims with practically same grounds); (ii) when comparing to prior art, indicate which parts of reference correspond to claimed features; (iii) if multiple prior art references used, select and describe the closest prior art, state differences between claim and closest reference, and explain how other references supplement those differences considering common general knowledge; (iv) examiner may specify prior art and present assessment regarding inventive step in terms applicants can understand; (v) state grounds for independent and dependent claims separately; dependent claims' grounds generally include all grounds cited in claims they depend on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of component comparison table
rubrics_metrics.description: Where necessary for comparing claims and prior art, prepare a component comparison table showing relations between distinguishing technical components of the claimed invention and corresponding features of the prior art reference, including where corresponding features are written in the cited document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table may include the claim element, the corresponding element in each prior art reference, and locations (page/drawing). Examiner may add judgments about differences within or below the table. Examples provided show mapping of A, B, C elements to prior-art counterparts and narrative assessment of obviousness or combination of references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations of Amendment content and limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Considerations of Amendment' states matters not grounds for rejection but useful for applicant response (e.g., examiner opinions on description, reasons for not listing certain claims as patentable, considerations for amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are advisory and intended to help applicants respond. If examiner later intends to rely on this content as a ground, the examiner must re-notify it as a formal ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of written decision to reject: structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A written decision to reject is prepared similarly to the written notice of grounds, except 'a matter notified for the ground for rejection' is replaced with 'a matter where the ground for rejection is not overcome'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sections include 'Claims to be Examined', 'Relevant Provisions for Matters Where Grounds for Rejection Not Overcome', 'Patentable Claims', 'Grounds for Decision to Reject', and 'Considerations in Amendment Submission'. If no written argument or amendment was submitted, examiner may not separately state 'Examination Results' and 'Rationale for Decision to Reject'. Newly added claims identical to previously-notified rejected claims may be included among matters where grounds are not overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Decision to Reject: content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Grounds for Decision to Reject' should provide a more specific rationale regarding grounds not overcome so applicants better understand why rejection stands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If same reasons were already notified in written ground for rejection, examiner may avoid redundancy by indicating source. When applicant submits both written argument and amendment, state why amendment does not overcome the ground and why applicant's arguments cannot be admitted. If only written argument submitted without amendment, explain why applicant's argument is denied and list unresolved grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in amendment submission at decision stage
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Considerations in Amendment Submission' states issues not grounds for rejection but useful for amendment submissions in subsequent procedures (e.g., reexamination requests).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if decision to reject is rendered but new grounds arise due to addition of claims or amendment, list such considerations to assist applicant in later procedures. This helps applicants plan deletions or further amendments when requesting reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Including claims affected by description deficiencies under Patentable Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the description has deficiencies, claims that seem related to such deficiency but do not themselves contain grounds for rejection can be classified under 'Patentable Claims', except where it is difficult to judge patentability upon the notice, or where a claim is related to the notified deficiency and an examiner judges amendment cannot remedy it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional cases where these claims are not included as patentable, explain in 'Considerations of Amendment' why they were excluded to assist applicant response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to citing claims when cited claim has ground (Article 42(4) situation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim cites another claim that has a ground for rejection under Article 42(4), the examiner must pay special attention to whether the citing claim still has such a ground. If so, state that the citing claim has the same ground for patent rejection as the cited claim. If the cited claim only violates manner of describing claims (Article 42(8)), then state only the cited claim has that ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly analyze whether dependence transmits the ground for rejection; state conclusions clearly in the notice to avoid applicant confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling multiple groups of inventions and unity-of-invention objections
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining applications with two or more groups of inventions, the examiner normally considers patentability for inventions in at least one group. When pointing out a violation of unity of invention, indicate claims in another group rather than the group already evaluated for patentability. Include claims without grounds under 'Patentable Claims' among evaluated groups; if novelty/inventive step rejections exist, notify those grounds together with unity objections for the other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary to notify lack of unity first for efficiency, state in 'Considerations of Amendment' that patentability tests were not performed for the unexamined group and do not include those claims in 'Patentable Claims'. This clarifies scope and prevents misleading applicants about which claims were fully examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior art documents: citation requirement and standard
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing grounds for rejection related to a claim's technical subject matter, the examiner shall cite supporting documents for the rationale. Disclosure methods for information on prior art documents shall comply with WIPO Standard ST.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always cite supporting prior art documents; follow WIPO ST.14 for disclosure methods not detailed here. Provide sufficient bibliographic detail so applicants can locate and understand the cited references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of patent documents: bibliographic format and specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing patent documents as supporting grounds, state the publishing country (can be omitted if Korea), title of patent document, document number (laid-open number), and publication date (public disclosure date if published in patent gazette).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and document number should match the cited patent document. Where parts of patent documents are used, clearly state page and drawing numbers in parentheses. Provide examples showing formats for Korea, US, JP, UK, DE, and international publications. Include classification notations for older German documents or abstract classifications when citing abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of non-patent literature: format rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-patent documents (periodicals, non-periodicals, books, etc.) should be cited with author name, thesis/title, publication title, location: publisher, publication date, volume/issue, page numbers, following detailed punctuation/format rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules include: (i) order and punctuation (author. title. publication: location: publisher. date, volume, issue, pp.); (ii) avoid abbreviations for publication titles; (iii) use 'Vol. oo, No. oo' for English; (iv) omit volume/issue when publication date suffices; (v) month/year if exact day not given; (vi) explain unclear publication dates; (vii) omit publisher when unnecessary; (viii) rules for location notation (omit for Korea), and (ix) page number notation with 'pp.' and hyphen/comma rules for ranges vs discontinuous pages. For books: author/editor. book title. location: publisher. date, volume/edition/page(s). Translated works include translator; book titles italicized. Examples in text illustrate journal and book citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of electronic documents: required metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic documents (CD-ROM, internet, online DB), state general bibliographic information along with the type of search medium (in braces), search date (in braces after publication date), and search site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details sufficient to reproduce the search and to locate the cited item. Example formats demonstrate including medium type and search date/site so applicants can retrieve the cited electronic source.
